text:
Marta R.: quick follow-up from the hybrid-ephemeral-pools RFC run earlier today — saw a couple of tail spikes when many tiny allocations got offloaded in burst. wondering if we should tighten the demote window or change prefetch pacing.

Leo K.: saw that too. spikes were ~40-60ms extra on tail for small batches (1-4 tokens). looks correlated with concurrent offload + nvme queue floods.

Cheng: do we have an easy repro? logs or a minimal trace would help.

Marta R.: repro is in the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/hybrid-pool/2026-03-19/tiny-offload-burst.tar.gz. quick trace excerpt: `offload_enqueue -> nvme-wait -> dequeue -> prefetch-miss` repeated.

Leo K.: thanks. my hypothesis: prefetch is being triggered synchronously during request completion for small pages because the KV cache marks them stale; that blocks the fast-path worker.

Sam: could we convert that prefetch to async background work with a soft backoff for small allocations? keep sync prefetch for large pages only.

Cheng: async helps but we need admission control to avoid nvme queue saturation. proposal: add a per-pool in-flight prefetch cap + exponential backoff. if cap exceeded, mark page as "lazy-demote" and rely on next request to fetch.

Marta R.: that sounds reasonable. tradeoff is increased miss latency for edge cases vs avoiding tail spikes. prefer a tunable knob so Dedicated customers can opt-in for lower tail at cost of some miss latency.

Leo K.: agree. another lever: increase small-page batching during offload so we coalesce many tiny pages into one NVMe IO. requires transient merge layer in the offload path. cost: some CPU and memory to buffer. benefit: amortize IOPS.

Sam: sketch of config we could expose:
```
pool:
  prefetch:
    in_flight_cap: 8
    async_small_pages: true
    small_page_batch_size: 16
    backoff_ms: 10
```

Cheng: +1. For observability, we need new metrics: prefetch_inflight, prefetch_backoff_count, small_page_coalesce_hits, nvme_queue_latency_p50/p95/p99. Add tags for pool_id and tenant.

Marta R.: can someone add a quick RFC follow-up PR that enumerates knobs and default values + a short experiment plan? I can run a canary on one dedicated pool.

Leo K.: I'll draft the PR. plan: A/B on a couple of workloads: small-chat burst (1-4 tokens) and long-form generation. measure tail p99 and overall token throughput.

Cheng: one more idea: for ephemeral pools we can increase the demote-window for tiny pages (so they stay resident longer), avoiding offload churn. downside: higher resident memory. make it tenant-configurable.

Sam: maybe combine both: slightly longer demote-window + async bounded prefetch + coalescing. seems robust.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/hybrid-prefetch-2026-03-24 02:00 UTC — infra job created by Leo K.. :rocket:

Marta R.: awesome. thx all. tagging @eng-sre for watch during canary. if we see nvme queue depth > 80% for >30s, auto-rollback.

Leo K.: PR link will follow in thread.

Cheng: posting a short checklist in the PR for metrics dashboards and alerts.

Sam: I'll update the Optimize recommendation docs after we have stable defaults.

Marta R.: perfect. end of thread for now — follow-up in PR and canary results. :thumbsup:
